races.note: OPEN SEAT: THE NEW CD1 LIES WHOLLY INSIDE SALT LAKE COUNTY UNDER COURT-DRAWN MAP 1A, and it is the only Democratic-leaning U.S. House seat Utah has. ✅ The Utah Supreme Court dismissed the Legislature's appeal Feb 20, 2026 and a federal three-judge panel refused to block the map Feb 23, so the map is final for 2026. ⚠ Cook PVI D+12, and Harris carried this territory by roughly 24 points [Verify — PVI via Wikipedia's Cook table, corroborated by Deseret News; Cook's own site returned 403]. ⚠ Ben McAdams won the June 23 primary with 51.90%, 29,737 of 57,295 [Verify — the state feed was still marked unofficial when pulled].

candidates.name: Ben McAdams
positions: Save the Great Salt Lake as top priority
Lower housing and health care costs
Protect and expand Affordable Care Act coverage
differentiators: Former one-term U.S. Representative, 2019-2021, old UT-4
Former two-term Salt Lake County mayor
Lost the Democratic convention, then qualified by signature
Raised about 2.26 million dollars through June 30, 2026
supporters: Say his county-mayor record shows he can actually deliver on housing and the lake.
Argue a proven moderate is the safest fit for a blue-but-not-deep-blue seat.
Point to a roughly 17-to-1 fundraising edge as evidence of broad backing.
opponents: Argue he is a retread who already lost a House seat to Burgess Owens in 2020.
Progressives say his centrism, including hedging on impeachment, blunts the message.
Note he lost the Democratic convention vote to Liban Mohamed before petitioning on.

candidates.name: Riley Owen
positions: Term limits and an age cap for Congress
Ban congressional stock trading
Tax credits for employer-paid maternity leave
differentiators: 27-year-old Naval Reserve intelligence officer
Former Trump White House policy staffer
Won the GOP convention outright with 71.2 percent
Calls his approach community conservatism
supporters: Say a young reform-minded Republican can win over unaffiliated Salt Lake voters.
Point to his convention landslide as evidence the party is unified behind him.
Argue Utah Republicans downballot still run well ahead of Trump in this district.
opponents: Had about 9,500 dollars cash on hand to McAdams' 300,000 [Verify — Deseret News, Aug 11, 2026].
Say a Trump White House resume is a liability in a district Harris carried decisively.
Note he has never held elected office.

candidates.name: Jesse West
positions: Stop funding foreign wars with U.S. tax dollars
Shrink the federal government's reach into daily life
Keep congressional focus on Utah's own priorities
differentiators: Salt Lake County family law attorney
Vice chair of the Salt Lake County Libertarian Party
Campaign slogan is Ski, Not War
Nominated at the Libertarian convention on April 18, 2026
supporters: Offer an explicitly antiwar choice for voters unhappy with both major parties.
Say a convention-only, low-cost campaign keeps him free of donor obligations [Verify — structural argument].
opponents: FEC totals show no reported fundraising through June 30, 2026.
No Utah Libertarian has ever come close to winning a U.S. House seat [Verify — structural argument].

candidates.name: Elias Henry Montgomery
positions: Legalize duplexes and townhomes to expand housing supply
Independent redistricting to end gerrymandering
A universal catastrophic health coverage floor
differentiators: Unaffiliated graduate researcher and data analyst [Verify — self-described on his campaign site]
Would shift federal income taxation to the states over ten years
Wants omnibus bills replaced with real-time public spending tracking
Runs with no party organization behind him
supporters: Say his structural reform agenda is more concrete than either major party's [Verify — self-described on his campaign site].
Argue an independent gives Utahns a genuine choice outside the red-blue split [Verify — structural argument].
opponents: No FEC fundraising record for his campaign could be located [Verify — an absence of located records].
Devolving federal income tax to the states sits far outside both parties' mainstream [Verify — structural argument].

races.note: BLAKE MOORE DID NOT CHOOSE TO SWITCH SEATS: MAP 1A RENUMBERED HIS NORTHERN UTAH DISTRICT FROM 1 TO 2. It gained Davis County and lost Morgan and Summit. ⚠ Celeste Maloy, the old CD2 incumbent, was drawn into CD3, so Utah's numbering shifted one seat down the line. ✅ Moore beat state Rep. Karianne Lisonbee 56.67% to 43.33% on June 23 [Verify — the state feed was still marked unofficial when pulled]. ⚠ Cook PVI R+15 [Verify — via Wikipedia's Cook table; Cook's own site returned 403]; Inside Elections baselines it R+38, Solid Republican [Verify — headline figure only, the page returned 403].

uncertainties: ⚠ THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS PARTLY WRONG AND WAS REFUTED: Blake Moore did NOT leave CD1 as a strategic choice. Map 1A RENUMBERED his northern Utah district from 1 to 2 (Deseret News, Apr 20, 2026) — it gained Davis County and lost Morgan and Summit. He filed for CD2 in the March 2026 window. Maloy, the old CD2 incumbent, was drawn into CD3.

Official status of the June 23 primary figures is UNCONFIRMED. Utah law has the lieutenant governor canvass multicounty races at noon on the fourth Monday after the primary (July 20, 2026) and certify to county clerks by Aug 1, which implies certification — but electionresults.utah.gov could not be loaded to confirm the flag flipped. Every primary figure carries [Verify].

The brief's July 8, 2026 dismissal of Powers Gardner v. Henderson could NOT be confirmed. The Feb 20, 2026 Utah Supreme Court dismissal and the February 2026 federal panel refusal WERE confirmed, so the note claims only that the map is final for 2026.
Write-in Babak (Bobby) Darvish is listed for CD1 by The Green Papers and by the state list. Write-ins are not printed on the ballot, so he is deliberately excluded from the candidate array.
New-map Cook PVI (CD1 D+12, CD2 R+15) comes from Wikipedia's 2026 PVI table; CD1 is independently corroborated by Deseret News. Treat CD2's R+15 as the weaker of the two. Both carry [Verify].

Cottam, Bowen and Moesinger have NO locatable campaign platform after two query formulations each. Their positions arrays are labelled party-platform placeholders or honest absence statements, not summaries of anything they said.
FEC figures are receipts through June 30, 2026 (Q2). The API returned null for cash on hand, so the CD1 cash-on-hand comparison is Deseret News reporting, not a direct FEC read.

Confirmed as briefed: McAdams is a former one-term U.S. Rep (2019-2021) and former Salt Lake County mayor who lost to Burgess Owens; Nate Blouin is a sitting state senator; Karianne Lisonbee is a sitting state representative and House majority whip.
